newsitem.title: UK: Britain's NFC year profits move ahead, dividend flat.
newsitem.headline: Britain's NFC year profits move ahead, dividend flat.

text.p: British transport-to-logistics group NFC Plc saw year pretax profits power ahead on Wednesday to 105.7 million pounds ($175 million), up 39 percent before exceptional items.

The annual dividend remained flat at 7.1 pence per share and sales were up 12 percent to 2.46 billion pounds, boosted by recent acquisitions. Underlying sales growth levels for the year ended September 30 was a more modest five percent.

The group, which has operations spanning Europe, the U.S. and Asia-Pacific, warned that market conditions remained "challenging", especially in Europe. But NFC said it was well poised to exploit any growth opportunities available.
Restructuring of its business is set to finish this financial year, with the benefits already reported to be feeding through.
Looking at a group breakdown of the results, the UK and Ireland division saw sales up 12 percent at 1.2 billion sterling, with profits up 28 percent to 78.3 million.

Strong business areas included the automotive business and TankFreight, but truck rental was described as less satisfactory. The grocery industry business turned in better profits, but margins on some contracts remained pressured.
Continental Europe saw sales up 22 percent to 373.4 million pounds, producing a loss of 8.5 million versus a 10.1 million loss last year.
The European logistics unit saw sales up 14 percent and a narrowing of losses by three percent. The German loss level was flat after cutting staff and withdrawing from frozen food delivery.

But the French chill network business was "disappointing" with a worsening of market conditions during the year and fuel price rises also hitting costs. The truck drivers' strike since the financial year-end cost NFC 500,000 pounds and hit margins.
But the Spanish and Portuguese markets were more robust with all divisions making "significant strides forward."
North American sales were up seven percent to 767.2 million, with profits up 73 percent to 25.5 million.
Excel Logistics sales were boosted by new business plus increased volumes from existing customers.
Other international operations saw sales up 16 percent to 111.7 million, with profits up 40 percent to six million.

The group is establishing an Asia-Pacific headquarters in Singapore, saying, "This anticipates significant growth opportunities as existing group customers in Europe and North America increase their sourcing and marketing activities in Asi-Pacific."
NFC shares remained flat on the news which reflected market expectations. At 1000 GMT the shares were up half a pence at 180 1/2 in a generally lower London market. ($1=.6047 Pound)
